memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb. The first to come out was red, and his whole body was like a hairy garment; so they named him Esau. After this, his brother came out, with his hand grasping Esau's heel; so he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them." - Gen 25:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long wait is over, and twins are born. The first is red and hairy, so he is named Esau. The second comes out gripping his brother's heel, so he is named Jacob — a name that hints at "one who grasps" or "supplanter." Even from birth these two are marked as different, and their names foreshadow the struggle to come.

It is striking that God's chosen line would run through Jacob — the grasping one, the younger, the one who would later scheme and stumble his way through life. Jacob was no polished saint. Yet God chose to work through him. This is grace: God does not wait for perfect people. He takes flawed, struggling, grasping people and shapes them for His purposes.

That should encourage every one of us. If God only used the impressive and the flawless, none of us would qualify. But the God of Jacob delights to take ordinary, imperfect people and make something beautiful of them (1 Cor 1:27-29). The line from Jacob would run all the way to Christ (Matt 1:2) — proof that God writes His story of redemption through unlikely hands.

Whatever your name has come to mean, God can give you a new story.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God can use me despite my flaws?
2. Where have I disqualified myself that God has not?
3. How does God's choice of Jacob encourage me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You work through flawed and unlikely people. Take my imperfect life and shape it for Your purposes, as You did with Jacob. Amen.
